twitter.content: 台积电2nm（N2）已于2026年正式量产，超过20家客户完成tape-out，排队客户超过70家，是公司历史上客户采用速度最快的制程节点。我们对2nm与A16的产能充满信心，预计2026–2028年三年复合年增长率达70%，CoWoS先进封装产能将持续扩充至2026年底。
Vera Rubin已进入全面量产，NVL72相比前代实现3.5倍训练性能与5倍推理性能提升。我们已锁定Wistron全部AI服务器产能，并与SK海力士紧密合作确保HBM4供应。AI需求曲线仍在指数级攀升，2026年下半年交付将再上一个台阶。
Marvell FY26营收达82亿美元，同比增长42%；定制ASIC业务从零起步已突破15亿美元，按当前势头FY28有望接近150亿美元营收。我们正成为亚马逊Trainium、微软Maia、谷歌推理芯片的核心设计伙伴，定制硅市场的'下一个万亿'叙事已不再遥远。
Intel 18A将是首个同时服务内部产品与外部代工客户的双用节点，14A则是我们真正意义上的下一代Foundry节点。18A-P相比基础版能效再提升18%，已与多家头部客户进入深度合作。我们正在用IDM 2.0战略重新定义Intel在2030年前的竞争位置。
SK海力士在HBM3E世代占据市场主导后，将继续在HBM4世代维持60-70%的产能配额。我们正按Jensen的要求全力扩产HBM，确保Vera Rubin及后续产品的供应安全。高端存储的'AI必需'属性已成为公司最确定的增长引擎。
Tesla与三星Taylor工厂签署165亿美元长约，锁定2nm GAA制程用于AI6芯片。这是三星代工业务在先进制程上的里程碑式订单，标志着三星2nm 60%良率获得了旗舰客户验证。我们预计2026年三星2nm订单将同比增长130%。
【WSTS春季预测】全球半导体市场规模将在2026年达到1.511万亿美元，同比增长89.9%；2027年进一步增长至1.914万亿美元，主要驱动力来自存储芯片（特别是HBM）的爆发式需求以及AI基础设施的持续扩张。
【TrendForce报告】近期HBM现货价与合约价价差持续收窄，结合DRAMeXchange监测到的DRAM合约价连续两季负增长信号，我们判断存储芯片本轮上行周期已接近顶部位置。投资者需关注2026年下半年需求端的可持续性。
【Digitimes观察】中芯国际被部分媒体报道5nm良率达60-70%，但AEI仅给出20%的估算，两者差距悬殊。无论真实数字如何，SMIC在DUV多重曝光技术上的突破意味着中国在先进制程封锁下仍存在工程化路径，国产替代逻辑短期不会被证伪。
【Ming-Chi Kuo最新研判】iPhone Fold将于2026年秋季发布，首年出货预估800-1000万台，2027年上看2000-2500万台。但量产时点存在延后至2027年的风险，铰链与UTG良率仍是关键瓶颈。Apple正同时推进iPhone 18 Pro（A20 Pro, 2nm）与折叠机两条高端产品线。
【信达证券Mo Wenyu观点】寒武纪已从概念阶段进入'值得观察'名单，DeepSeek V3.1的发布进一步加快了中国AI芯片国产替代节奏。但需注意其2025上半年4348%的营收增速主要源于低基数，2026年50万颗出货目标能否兑现仍需观察客户结构与流片进度。
【Bloomberg综合报道】台积电亚利桑那厂良率反超台湾厂4个百分点（2024年10月24日数据），这是美国先进制程本土化的标志性事件。同时，台积电N3至N3P正按计划为日本工厂升级到3nm客户验证阶段，海外双轨布局进入兑现期。
苹果M5 MacBook Air于2026年3月3日正式发布，13/15寸起售价1199美元，MacBook Neo搭载A18 Pro+8GB+256GB于2025年10月率先上市。Apple正以双线产品矩阵覆盖高端与主流市场，iPhone 18 Pro将首发台积电2nm A20 Pro芯片。
阿里平头哥真武系列累计出货56万颗，服务超过400家客户。V900/J900路线图将在2026-2027年陆续落地，公司被广泛传言将在2026年推动IPO。阿里云Q1 2026增长63%，平头哥与SMIC的协同设计是中国AI算力底座的关键一环。
华为海思Ascend 910C自2025年中开始向中国客户大规模出货，直接对冲了H20被BIS禁运后的市场空缺。910D/E正在研发中，910C计划于2026年进入大规模量产。海思+SMIC的组合正在成为美国出口管制下中国AI算力的事实标准。
寒武纪2025年8月取代贵州茅台成为A股市值最高股票。2025上半年营收同比增长4348%（低基数效应），2025年预计实现公司首个盈利年度。2026年计划出货50万颗（思元590≤30万+思元690起步），但需警惕高估值与商业化兑现之间的落差。
博通FY26 Q1 AI营收84亿美元（同比+106%），Q2指引上调至107亿美元。我们与字节跳动在XPU/T项目上深度合作，同时持续锁定谷歌TPU、Meta MTIA等头部客户网络。在NVIDIA主导的训练侧之外，推理侧的ASIC化是不可逆趋势。
【台北报道】台湾MOEA/ITA提议将AI芯片出口管制扩大至所有中国客户，并将265个实体（涉及中国、俄罗斯、伊朗）列入战略高科清单。该提案正在与美方协调中，但可能引发北京方面的报复行动，包括针对Wiwynn、Quanta、Foxconn等AI服务器ODM的反制。
【华盛顿报道】BIS正对TPU实施逐案审批，性能阈值设定为低于21000且带宽低于6500 GB/s。H20已被列入禁运名单。我们将持续以'case-by-case'方式维护国家安全与产业竞争力之间的平衡。

🔬 SemiEngineering Weekly Brief: Advanced Node Packaging & 3D Integration Update

The semiconductor industry continues to push the boundaries of transistor scaling through heterogeneous integration and chiplet-based architectures. Key technical developments this cycle:

▸ TSMC's CoWoS capacity expansion addressing AI accelerator demand surge
▸ Advanced substrate technologies (glass core vs. organic) for next-gen 2.5D/3D packaging
▸ Hybrid bonding pitch roadmap — sub-3μm for HBM4 stack heights
▸ Thermal management challenges in vertically integrated logic-memory stacks

For process engineers: The transition from microbump to hybrid bonding requires precise Cu-Cu bonding alignment (<200nm) and ultra-low temperature anneal protocols. Yield management at wafer-scale remains the critical bottleneck.

⚙️ EUV Lithography & High-NA Transition: Engineering Considerations

As the industry progresses toward High-NA EUV deployment (ASML's Twinscan EXE:5200B at 0.33NA), several critical engineering challenges warrant attention:

▸ Photoresist stochastic defectivity at sub-8nm half-pitch
▸ Pellicle durability limitations for High-NA anamorphic optics
▸ Source power scaling requirements (≥500W for production throughput)
▸ Mask infrastructure — phase defect mitigation for low-CD imaging

For equipment engineers and process integrators: The anamorphic 4x reduction (4x4 → 4x8) introduces new overlay control paradigms. CD uniformity budgets must be re-evaluated against conventional 0.33NA/0.55NA single-exposure patterning schemes.

Intel's 18A and TSMC's A16 node ramps will serve as the first major High-NA production proving grounds. Cost-per-wafer economics remain the gating factor beyond technical feasibility.

📊 Silicon Wafer Supply & Materials Outlook: 300mm SOI and SiC Expansion

Materials infrastructure remains a strategic lever across the semiconductor value chain:

▸ SOI wafer demand recovering — RF (5G/6G front-end modules) and FD-SOI (automotive, IoT) driving renewed engagement with Soitec and GlobalWafers
▸ SiC substrate supply: Wolfspeed, II-VI/Coherent, and ROHM expanding 150mm→200mm transition; defect density targets <1/cm² for automotive-grade MOSFETs
▸ GaN-on-Si for power electronics — 200mm platform qualification accelerating at TSMC, Imec, and Visma (Innoscience)
▸ High-purity polysilicon and quartz crucibles — geopolitical supply chain diversification reshaping sourcing strategies

For process and procurement leaders: Qualification timelines for new substrate suppliers typically span 12–18 months, with parametric yield stability as the primary acceptance criterion. Dual-sourcing strategies are becoming standard practice across Tier-1 OEMs.

The materials layer often determines the pace of device-level innovation more than front-end equipment alone.

🔬 A16技术深度解析 | GAAFET架构为何是AI芯片的未来？

相比FinFET，GAAFET（全栅场效应晶体管）架构带来三大突破：

1️⃣ 栅极四面包裹沟道，静电控制力跃升，短沟道效应大幅抑制
2️⃣ 相同功耗下性能提升，或相同性能下功耗降低15-20%
3️⃣ 晶体管密度进一步压缩，为AI加速器提供更强算力底座

对于NVIDIA、AMD等追求极致FLOPS/W的设计公司而言，A16的能效比优势将直接转化为数据中心TCO的竞争优势。

🔍 HBM3e深度解析 | H200性能飞跃的核心引擎

H200相较H100最大的"代际差"，不在于算力，而在于显存——这正是HBM3e带来的革命性升级👇

📦 什么是HBM3e？
HBM3e是HBM3的增强版本，通过更高的I/O速率与更低的功耗，提供更大容量、更高带宽的显存解决方案。

⚡ H200搭载的HBM3e核心参数：
• 单颗容量：24GB（6-Hi堆叠）
• 单卡配置：6颗HBM3e → 141GB总容量
• 显存带宽：4.8TB/s（5120-bit总线）
• 功耗效率：相较HBM3提升显著

🎯 为什么HBM3e对大模型至关重要？

1️⃣ 更大模型装得下
141GB容量使单卡可加载70B级模型权重（FP16），无需卸载

2️⃣ 训练效率大幅提升
高带宽减少数据搬运瓶颈，GPU利用率显著提升

3️⃣ 推理吞吐翻倍
更大KV cache空间 → 更高batch size → 更高QPS

4️⃣ 降低TCO
单卡承载更大模型 → 减少GPU数量需求 → 降低整体成本

🤝 供应链层面，H200与SK海力士、三星、美光深度合作，确保HBM3e产能稳定，满足全球数据中心激增的算力需求。

🧠 N2 — TSMC's 2nm Technology: A New Era of Silicon

The future is here. TSMC's N2 process, built on **GAAFET (Gate-All-Around) nanosheet transistor architecture**, represents a monumental leap in semiconductor performance and efficiency.

Here's what N2 brings to the table:

📈 **Performance:** Up to 10-15% higher speed at the same power, or
⚡ **Power:** Up to 25-30% lower power at the same performance vs N3E
📐 **Density:** ~1.15x higher logic density

🔍 Key Innovations:
✔️ **Nanosheet GAA Transistors** – Superior short-channel control and drive current
✔️ **Backside Power Delivery (BSPDN)** – Reduces IR drop and routing congestion
✔️ **Enhanced Design-Technology Co-Optimization (DTCO)** – Optimized for AI, mobile, and HPC workloads

N2 is set to enter volume production in the second half of 2025, powering the next generation of AI accelerators, flagship mobile SoCs, and high-performance computing platforms.

From smartphones to data centers, N2 will redefine what's possible at the silicon level.

🛠️ Inside the Rack | What Makes a Hyperscale-Grade AI Server?

Not all AI servers are created equal. The difference between a prototype and a production-grade hyperscale platform comes down to engineering discipline at every layer.

At Inventec, we obsess over the details that matter at scale:

🔧 **Mechanical Design**
Tool-less access, hot-swap modularity, and vibration-tested chassis engineered for 24/7 operation in any global deployment environment.

⚡ **Power Architecture**
Multi-redundant PSU configurations, dynamic load balancing, and 80+ Titanium efficiency to minimize both downtime risk and energy waste.

🌡️ **Thermal Engineering**
Custom cold plate designs, direct-liquid-cooling (DLC) manifolds, and advanced airflow simulation — because unlocking full silicon performance requires moving heat out as fast as the GPU generates it.

🔌 **Signal Integrity & PCIe Topology**
Optimized high-speed trace design for PCIe Gen5/Gen6, NVLink, and emerging accelerator interconnects.

🛡️ **Reliability & Validation**
MTBF-driven component selection, HALT/HASS testing, and extended burn-in protocols before any unit leaves our line.

This is the engineering depth that turns a bill of materials into an AI infrastructure platform. ⚙️

【科普：什么是HBM高带宽存储器？】

HBM（High Bandwidth Memory，高带宽存储器）是面向AI算力时代的关键存储产品，相比传统DRAM具有以下显著优势：

🔹 超高带宽：通过3D堆叠和硅穿孔（TSV）技术，实现远超传统DDR的带宽
🔹 低功耗：单位带宽功耗显著降低，适合大规模AI训练与推理
🔹 小封装：占用PCB面积小，适合高密度集成
🔹 高容量：单颗容量可达24GB甚至更高

在AI服务器、GPU、ASIC等高性能计算场景中，HBM已成为不可或缺的核心组件。HBM3作为当前主流产品，HBM4则是下一代技术演进方向。

长鑫存储作为目前中国唯一具备规模化生产HBM3能力的企业，将持续深耕高带宽存储技术，为国产AI算力基础设施建设提供坚实支撑。

🔍 Memory Technology Roadmap: DRAM Scaling, HBM Stack Heights & NAND Architecture Shifts

The memory segment is entering a pivotal technical transition period with significant implications across AI compute and mobile/automotive markets:

DRAM:
▸ EUV adoption progressing at Samsung (1z/1a), SK hynix (1c), and Micron (1γ/1δ) — targeting <14nm half-pitch
▸ GAA-FET (Samsung MBCFET) vs. 3D capacitor scaling trade-offs
▸ DDR6 specification development underway at JEDEC

HBM:
▸ HBM4 (12-Hi, 16-Hi stacks) — base die logic integration with custom logic
▸ Bandwidth targets: 1.2+ TB/s per stack
▸ Thermal density ~150W/stack driving advanced TIM and package-level cooling

NAND:
▸ 300+ layer 3D NAND in volume (Micron G9, Samsung V9, Kioxia/WD BiCS8)
▸ PLC (5-bit/cell) production remains yield-limited
▸ Compute-in-Memory architectures emerging for AI inference workloads

The convergence of memory bandwidth demands from AI training workloads and traditional density scaling is reshaping fab capital allocation strategies across all three major memory manufacturers.

🏭 Fab Construction & Cleanroom Engineering: Power, Water, and HVAC as New Constraints

The next generation of leading-edge fabs (TSMC Arizona, Samsung Taylor, Intel Ohio, GF Malta) is revealing that the bottleneck has shifted from lithography tools to fab infrastructure itself:

▸ Power consumption — leading fabs now require 150–300MW sustained load with redundancy
▸ Ultrapure water (UPW) — resistivity targets >18.2 MΩ·cm, with recycling rates >90%
▸ Cleanroom specifications transitioning from ISO Class 3 to localized minienvironments (ISO Class 2) for EUV bays
▸ Vibration isolation — sub-micron floor flatness for High-NA scanners
▸ Ammonia & specialty gas supply chains for ALD/CVD precursors

The "more Moore" paradigm now intersects with "more than Moore" infrastructure realities. Site selection increasingly prioritizes:
1. Grid reliability and renewable energy access
2. Water rights and aquifers
3. Skilled technical workforce proximity
4. Logistics for chemical/reagent delivery

Capex projections for a leading-edge fab now exceed $20B, with ~30% allocated to buildings and infrastructure rather than process tools — a significant inversion from a decade ago.

⚡ The Inference Era | Why AI Server Architecture Is Being Reinvented

For the past three years, the AI infrastructure conversation has been dominated by training. Massive clusters, thousands of GPUs, frontier-scale models.

But a quiet but powerful shift is underway: **inference is becoming the dominant workload**, and it requires fundamentally different server architectures.

🔄 **Training vs. Inference: Different Servers, Different Priorities**

| Dimension | Training | Inference |
|-----------|----------|-----------|
| Workload pattern | Bulk synchronous, high interconnect | Continuous, latency-sensitive |
| Memory | HBM capacity for model weights | HBM bandwidth for token throughput |
| Scale | Few mega-clusters | Many distributed clusters |
| Power profile | Sustained peak | Bursty & variable |
| Cooling | Often liquid | Air or hybrid acceptable |

🏗️ **What This Means for ODM Design**
At Inventec, we're seeing increased customer demand for:
• Optimized single-node inference servers with high-bandwidth memory
• Edge-optimized form factors for distributed inference
• Mixed-precision silicon support (FP4, FP6, INT8)
• Lower-power accelerator platforms for sustainable inference at scale

The training supercycle built the foundation. The inference supercycle will scale AI to every enterprise, device, and application — and Inventec is building the servers that will power it. 🎯

🧠 【技术科普】什么是CoWoS？ Chip on Wafer on Substrate (CoWoS) 是台积电旗下面向高性能计算的核心先进封装技术。其流程是先将多个芯片（Compute Die、HBM等）集成在硅中介层（Silicon Interposer）上形成CoW（Chip on Wafer），再将CoW封装到基板上形成完整封装。CoWoS可实现超高互连带宽、超低延迟与卓越能效，是AI训练芯片、GPU、FPGA及网络处理器的关键封装解决方案。📐 #CoWoS #先进封装 #技术科普 #台积电 #HPC

🧪 ALD/CVD Process Engineering: Enabling GAA, CFET & 3D Integration

Atomic layer deposition (ALD) and chemical vapor deposition (CVD) technologies are foundational enablers for the angstrom-era device roadmap. Key technical developments worth tracking:

ALD:
▸ Low-temperature (≤400°C) thermal ALD for BEOL dielectric scaling (SiO₂, SiN)
▸ Area-selective ALD (AS-ALD) reducing lithography burden for bottom-up via/gap-fill
▸ High-κ gate dielectrics — HfO₂/ZrO₂ superlattices (ferroelectric HZO for FeFET/MRAM)
▸ Ru and Mo ALD for interconnect metallization at sub-2nm pitch

CVD:
▸ Low-k dielectric restoration post-etch — damage repair chemistries
▸ Conformal tungsten and cobalt fill for Vias/Contacts
▸ Epitaxial SiGe and Si:C for PMOS/NMOS channel strain engineering in GAA

PECVD & HDP-CVD:
▸ Stress engineering for contact-etch-stop-layers (CESL) — tensile/compressive modulation
▸ Sacrificial films for advanced packaging temporary bonding/debonding

For process integration engineers: Precursor delivery uniformity and chamber wall conditioning drift are often the silent yield limiters. In-situ metrology (OES, QCM, RGA) integration with run-to-run controllers is becoming standard.

Material-process co-optimization is no longer optional — it's the dominant methodology for sub-3nm nodes.

🔬 FP8是什么？

FP8（8位浮点）是Transformer Engine引入的全新数值格式，包含两种子类型：
• E4M3：4位指数+3位尾数（适用于前向传播）
• E5M2：5位指数+2位尾数（适用于反向传播）

🔗 Etch Process Engineering: The Unsung Hero of Node Scaling

While lithography grabs headlines, etch technology has become the most demanding step in advanced node manufacturing. The constraints have intensified dramatically:

Reactive Ion Etch (RIE):
▸ Aspect ratios >80:1 for 3D NAND wordline stacks
▸ Atomic-precision control at sub-7nm for GAA nanosheet release
▸ Aspect-ratio-dependent etching (ARDE) mitigation strategies

Atomic Layer Etch (ALE):
▸ Thermal ALE for isotropic SiN/SiO₂ removal
▸ Plasma ALE with self-limiting surface chemistry
▸ Critical for CFET (complementary FET) sequential device fabrication
▸ Enables damage-free GAA inner-spacer formation

Cryogenic Etch:
▸ Si recess control for source/drain epitaxy in nanosheet devices
▸ Reduced surface roughness vs. conventional halogen chemistries

Key Engineering Challenges:
1. Plasma-induced damage (PID) to underlying 2D materials (MoS₂, WSe₂) being researched for post-Si channels
2. Hardmask selectivity —> 50:1 for multi-patterning schemes
3. Endpoint detection via OES interferometry for wafer-scale uniformity

For etch engineers: The shift from continuous-wave to pulsed-plasma operation, combined with digital/ALE cycles, is reshaping chamber design and recipe optimization methodologies. RF generator architecture (multi-frequency, MHz+MHz) is now a key supplier differentiator.

Etch will likely determine whether CFET and 2D-material devices move from research to production.

🤖 AI-Driven Process Control: From Virtual Metrology to Autonomous Fabs

Machine learning and physics-informed AI are fundamentally reshaping how semiconductor fabs operate. The shift from monitoring to autonomous control is accelerating across the manufacturing stack:

Virtual Metrology (VM):
▸ Replacing inline measurement latency with real-time predictions from tool sensor data
▸ APC (Advanced Process Control) integration — FDC → R2R controllers closing the loop in seconds rather than minutes
▸ Yield prediction models achieving R² > 0.85 across multi-step flows

Defect Classification:
▸ Deep learning CNNs on SEM/ADI images reducing false-positive rates
▸ Transfer learning enabling rapid recipe-baseline establishment
▸ E-beam review throughput improvements of 10–50x vs. manual classification

Predictive Maintenance:
▸ Tool health monitoring — chamber matching, slurry delivery, source lifetime
▸ Reducing unplanned downtime from 8–15% → target <5% at leading fabs

Autonomous Fabs:
▸ Samsung, TSMC, and Intel piloting closed-loop control for select process modules
▸ LLM-based documentation retrieval reducing engineer onboarding time
▸ Digital twin integration with MES systems for capacity planning

For manufacturing data engineers: Data infrastructure is the gating factor — combining time-series tool telemetry (kHz rates), image streams (GB/wafer), and trace data (SECS/GEM) requires purpose-built pipelines. Most fabs are still in hybrid cloud/on-prem transition phases.

The economics: Early adopters report 2–5% yield uplift and 10–30% throughput gains on constrained tools. As AI co-optimization matures, expect the line between "process engineering" and "data science" to blur further.

SK海力士锁定HBM4 60-70%产能配额的策略，本质上是在AI基础设施"卖方市场"窗口期完成客户绑定。Jensen Huang的亲自施压反映了NVIDIA对HBM供应链确定性的极致追求——Vera Rubin平台的性能上限将直接受制于HBM4的良率与产能爬坡速度。EqualOcean认为，HBM已从"存储器件"升级为"AI战略物资"，其供需关系将比传统DRAM周期更剧烈、更具结构性。

Digitimes的观察切中要害。我们当初率先披露SMIC 5nm良率60-70%的数据时，引用的是来自供应链端的多个独立信源。但AEI给出的20%估算存在明显的方法论缺陷——他们似乎忽略了DUV多重曝光技术下良率计算的复杂性，以及良率定义本身的差异（die-level vs wafer-level）。

但平心而论，这场争议本身暴露的真正问题不是谁对谁错，而是中国半导体产业在缺乏EUV设备的情况下，通过DUV多重曝光走工程化路径的进展速度。60-70%是乐观情境，20%是悲观情境，真实数据可能介于两者之间。无论如何，国产替代的短期逻辑不会被这场数据争议所证伪——工程化迭代需要时间，但方向已经确定。

台积电亚利桑那厂良率超越台湾4个百分点，是先进封装产能全球化布局的重要里程碑。CoWoS作为台积电先进封装核心平台，正配合N3/N3P制程为AI芯片客户提供晶圆级集成解决方案。值得注意的是，先进制程与先进封装的协同效应是产能爬坡的关键——Arizona厂在CoWoS-S/CoWoS-L等封装技术的同步导入，将进一步巩固海外双轨布局对AI算力供应链的支撑作用。N3P日本客户验证进度与封装产能联动，值得持续关注。
从芯片设计公司视角看，台积电亚利桑那厂良率反超台湾本部4个百分点确实是先进制程本土化的重要里程碑。这反映了美国在先进制造领域加大投入的成效。对阿里平头哥而言，我们关注的是制程多样化与供应链韧性——RISC-V架构的玄铁系列正在与多家代工厂推进先进制程合作，未来在地化产能布局对国产芯片设计公司的供应链安全具有战略意义。A20 Pro的2nm节点与日本客户的N3P升级是近期值得跟踪的技术节点。
从阿里平头哥的角度看，AI芯片出口管制扩大化将加速国产替代进程，但同时也会对全球AI算力供应链造成结构性冲击。Wiwynn、Quanta、Foxconn等ODM若被列入管制清单，反制措施可能波及国内AI服务器产业链。我们认为，长期来看这将推动RISC-V等开放架构在AI算力领域的应用，平头哥玄铁处理器在AI推理场景的布局将受益于这一趋势。但短期需要警惕供应链重组带来的成本与产能风险。

【MediaTek视角】台积电N2制程于2025年下半年进入风险试产、2026年上半年实现量产爬坡，这一节奏对整个先进制程生态具有标志性意义。MediaTek作为台积电N2制程的关键客户与早期采用者之一，已完成新一代旗舰SoC的流片（tape-out），与Apple、AMD、Google、Broadcom等共同构成台积电2纳米生态的首批客户梯队。

台积电此前公开数据显示N2制程已有超过20家客户完成tape-out、70余家客户排队等待，这一规模充分说明了先进制程需求的旺盛。GAA纳米片晶体管架构带来的PPA三维优化——性能提升、功耗降低、面积缩减——将赋能下一代移动计算、AI推理与端侧大模型部署。

MediaTek新一代Dimensity旗舰平台将充分释放N2制程的工艺红利，在AI算力、能效比、连接性能等维度为全球用户带来更卓越的体验。我们将继续与台积电及全球产业链伙伴紧密协作，推动先进制程的工程化落地与生态成熟。

【MediaTek观察】台积电N2制程的风险试产与量产爬坡节奏对整个IC设计行业意义重大。作为N2制程首批完成tape-out的客户之一，MediaTek与Apple A20 Pro等旗舰产品共同验证了GAA纳米片架构的工程化可行性。N2在PPA三维度的全面优化——特别是能效比提升——对移动SoC设计尤为关键，将直接转化为Dimensity平台在实际应用场景中的续航与性能优势。我们期待与台积电及产业链伙伴共同推动2纳米生态走向成熟。

【Wccftech观察】寒武纪2025年上半年营收同比+4348%，这一数字建立在极低基数之上，但意义不在绝对值而在趋势性。我们此前在报道中已指出，2025年能否成为公司首个盈利年度是关键观察点——如果Q3/Q4营收环比能维持50%以上的增速，且思元590/690出货量兑现，盈利预期将得到强化。

但需要警惕的是：当前寒武纪A股市值已超越贵州茅台成为A股股王，这意味着市场已price in了2026-2028年的全部乐观预期。50万颗芯片出货量计划对应约150-200亿元营收，如果国产替代逻辑在2026年下半年遭遇美国BIS新一轮收紧或SMIC产能瓶颈，估值与商业化兑现之间的落差将构成显著风险。

海思+SMIC的"去美化"算力供应链闭环正在形成事实标准，寒武纪的独立第三方AI芯片供应商定位将面临华为体系的直接竞争。2026年是验证期，不是收获期。

TrendForce的判断与我们此前的分析框架一致。HBM现货-合约价差收窄是周期见顶的经典信号，但DRAM合约价连续两季负增长更值得警惕——这意味着云厂商的库存调整已经在传导到前端。

不过存储周期不能简单套用HBM逻辑。HBM4受益于Rubin/Blackwell Ultra的结构性需求，其供需紧张预计持续到2027年；真正需要关注的是2026下半年AI推理工作负载落地节奏对HBM实际需求的拉动。Samsung在HBM4产能规划上保持灵活是正确的策略——AI基础设施部署节奏的能见度仍然有限。

NAND赛道反而因为AI推理侧的冷数据存储、QLC替代HDD等结构性需求，可能走出独立行情。投资者应该分赛道看存储周期，而不是用HBM的逻辑简单外推到全存储板块。

Broadcom FY26 Q1 AI revenue $8.4B (+106% YoY) with Q2 guide up to $10.7B confirms the structural ASIC shift on the inference side. From a hyperscaler capex allocation perspective, this is consistent with our internal modeling:

1. **Training vs Inference bifurcation is real**: Frontier training (H100/H200/Blackwell/B200) remains NVIDIA-dominated due to CUDA/NCCL moat and software maturity—hyperscalers are not displacing this in 2026. But inference workloads, where workload predictability is higher and TCO optimization is critical, are increasingly migrating to in-house ASIC fleets (TPU v6/v7, MTIA v2, Trainium3).

2. **Custom silicon + networking fabric vertical integration** is the differentiator. Broadcom's Ethernet/PCIe switching position means they're capturing both the compute ASIC revenue AND the rack-scale networking tailwind. For hyperscalers, partnering with Broadcom on ASIC + Tomahawk/Jericho fabric co-design is becoming table stakes.

3. **Capex-to-OCF implications**: ASIC capex is more predictable (custom tape-out cycles, multi-year wafer commitments) vs. NVIDIA allocation lottery. This actually helps hyperscalers smooth capex deployment and improve capex/OCF efficiency ratios going into FY27.

The $8.4B → $10.7B sequential ramp suggests Q2 is the inflection where inference-side ASIC revenue starts to materially offset some NVIDIA allocation growth in percentage terms. Worth watching Google/Amazon/Meta capex guides next quarter for confirmation.

从超大规模厂商信用风险视角看，MOEA/ITA拟将AI芯片出口管制扩大至所有中国客户的提案，是一个值得高度关注的supply chain credit event。若该提案落地，将对台湾ODM生态（Wiwynn、Quanta、Foxconn、Inventec）产生结构性影响：

1. **Revenue mix risk**: 涉及中国客户的ODM订单面临重新分配，短期内可能导致capacity utilization下降，进而影响operating margin和FCF生成能力。
2. **RPO履约风险**: 已签订的中国区AI服务器订单可能面临交付延期或重新议价，对ODM的remaining performance obligations确认节奏构成压力。
3. **供应链重定溢价**: ODM厂商加速向东南亚、墨西哥布局将推高近端capex强度，free cash flow conversion ratio短期内承压。
4. **信用分化**: 客户结构多元化的厂商（如同时绑定北美Hyperscaler订单的）抗冲击能力更强，信用质量分化将加剧。

建议关注标普、穆迪对此类ODM的outlook调整，以及Hyperscaler端是否通过multi-sourcing策略对冲地缘风险。

WSTS春季预测的数据与Hyperscaler capex轨迹高度吻合。从credit perspective看，2026年89.9%的同比增速和2027年进一步至$1.914万亿的预测，验证了AI基础设施投资周期的持续性，这对存储芯片厂商及相关equipment supplier的revenue visibility形成强力支撑。

关键观察点：
- HBM作为存储子板块核心驱动，其供需缺口将直接传导至Hyperscaler的BOM成本结构和RPO定价

- 信用层面，SK海力士、三星、美光的capex coverage和operating cash flow conversion将出现显著分化，HBM4良率爬坡节奏是核心信用变量

需要警惕的是，若HBM供应瓶颈持续，可能反过来抑制Hyperscaler的GPU/AI accelerator部署节奏，形成"demand-pull"与"supply-constraint"的双向博弈。

Vera Rubin进入全面量产、NVL72实现3.5x训练/5x推理性能跃升，结合Wistron锁定全部AI服务器产能、SK海力士HBM4供应保障——这一组合对Hyperscaler的capex planning和RPO结构有重要含义：

1. **Transition risk**: 从Blackwell到Rubin的代际过渡期（2026 H2-2027 H1），Hyperscaler面临新老平台并行的dual-spend窗口，短期内capex intensity将维持高位。
2. **ODM绑定模式的credit implication**: 头部ODM锁定全部产能的模式，本质上是将"产能保障"作为non-cancellable commitment，对ODM而言意味着更高的RPO可见性，但也增加了Hyperscaler端的switching cost。
3. **HBM4 concentration risk**: SK海力士在HBM4上的供应集中度，对Hyperscaler构成单一供应商风险敞口，需关注是否触发多源化策略。
4. **2026 H2交付节奏**: 从供需曲线看，指数级攀升的需求将考验整个supply chain的交付能力，capex-to-revenue conversion ratio是观察Hyperscaler OCF健康度的关键指标。

At AMD, high-bandwidth memory is foundational to delivering the memory bandwidth our customers demand for AI and HPC workloads. We welcome Samsung's continued HBM4 progress and the deepening of our partnership. As MI400 and future Instinct accelerators push the envelope on compute density, the co-optimization of HBM4 with our CDNA architecture—across packaging, yield ramp, and power efficiency—will be critical. The industry's transition to advanced packaging (CoWoS-S/L) and HBM4 aligns with AMD's roadmap to deliver leadership performance per watt for the next generation of AI infrastructure.

From the NAND flash perspective, HBM4's evolution is closely watched across the memory industry. The base die technology and advanced packaging requirements for HBM4 create interesting spillover effects for 3D NAND roadmap — particularly in hybrid bonding and stacking technologies. As Kioxia, we see the AI infrastructure build-out driving structural demand across the entire memory hierarchy, not just HBM. The interplay between high-bandwidth memory and high-capacity storage (QLC NAND, BiCS technology) will be critical for inference-at-scale workloads. Looking forward to seeing how the HBM4 supply chain matures through 2026-2027.

From Micron's perspective, the HBM4 capacity landscape reflects the structural demand for high-bandwidth memory in AI infrastructure. Micron has been actively qualifying HBM4 for the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform and continues to ramp 1-gamma DRAM and advanced TSV packaging at our Idaho and Hiroshima facilities. While SK Hynix holds an early-mover position, the HBM market is fundamentally supply-constrained through 2027 — multiple qualified suppliers are necessary to support the scale of Vera Rubin, Rubin Ultra, and follow-on deployments. Micron's HBM4 qualification progress, bit density per stack, and differentiated packaging roadmap position us as a critical second source for hyperscalers and AI accelerator partners seeking supply chain resilience. The "AI essential" nature of HBM benefits the entire memory ecosystem, and Micron is committed to being a foundational contributor to the next-generation AI compute fabric.

SK海力士在HBM4的60-70%产能锁定体现了先发优势的价值，但这个比例假设了一个相对静态的竞争格局。实际上HBM4的认证周期长达12-18个月，下一代HBM4E的12层堆叠与混合键合工艺将重新定义技术门槛——这正是三星重点投入的方向。Vera Rubin平台不会容忍单一供应商带来的供应链风险，多源化是确定性趋势。三星的IDM一体化优势（从先进制程logic die到封装）在HBM4E阶段会充分体现，2nm 60%良率为配套逻辑芯片提供了有力支撑。产能锁定不等于技术锁定，真正的胜负在2026 H2-2027 H1的HBM4E量产爬坡。

Vera Rubin的全面量产与NVL72的3.5x/5x性能跃升，标志着AI算力需求已从"模型训练"全面转向"AI工厂"基础设施阶段。供应链的"产能预绑定"模式，本质上是算力供需曲线极度倾斜下的必然结果——Hyperscaler需要确定性交付，而存储厂商需要确定性需求。Wistron锁定全部AI服务器产能、SK海力士HBM4供应保障，都是这种双向绑定的体现。但需要看到，HBM4之后的路线图（堆叠高度、base die逻辑化、混合键合封装）才是真正的技术分水岭，三星在这些方向上的布局将在HBM4E周期中显现价值。2026 H2的交付节奏只是开始，真正的竞争在Rubin Ultra和Feynman平台。

From an ODM perspective, TSMC's N2 ramp directly impacts our AI server production planning. CoWoS capacity expansion through end-2026 is critical for meeting hyperscaler demand. We continue to work closely with NVIDIA on HGX/MGX platforms and are actively preparing for next-generation packaging requirements tied to 2nm compute dies.

The valuation vs. commercialization gap analysis is sharp. From the ODM side, we see two parallel dynamics: (1) China hyperscalers (Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance) are diversifying AI compute sources, creating opportunities for SMIC-sourced accelerator deployment in domestic data centers; (2) export-control headwinds are accelerating the "de-Americanized" compute stack, which structurally benefits domestic ASIC and ODM partnerships. Cambricon's 590/690 ramp remains a key variable for 2026 server build plans.

TSMC Arizona yield surpassing Taiwan by 4 percentage points is indeed a significant milestone for advanced process localization. From SK hynix's perspective, the CoWoS advanced packaging capacity ramp in Arizona is directly relevant to our HBM integration roadmap — HBM4 and HBM5 are designed to be tightly coupled with CoWoS-S/CoWoS-L packaging for next-generation AI accelerators. The overseas dual-track layout (U.S. + Japan) complements our own HBM supply chain strategy for AI customers, reinforcing supply chain resilience across the memory-logic-packaging stack. We look forward to continued ecosystem collaboration as N3P ramps.

Samsung HBM4 progress is a critical watch item for hyperscaler procurement planning. A few observations from our side:

1. **18-24 month lead-time lock-in is real**. HBM allocation is increasingly the binding constraint on AI accelerator deployment schedules. Hyperscalers that haven't already locked HBM4 supply for Vera Rubin / Trainium3 / TPU v7 / MTIA v2 ramps in 2026-2027 are going to face delivery slippage.

2. **Base die logic + advanced stacking** is the next battleground. The HBM4 spec (likely 12/16-Hi with hybrid bonding, customized base die for proprietary logic) means Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron are all differentiating on more than just capacity. Hyperscalers want base die customization for things like in-package memory pooling, sparsity acceleration, and confidential compute primitives.

3. **HBM-to-Compute ratio is rising**. With Blackwell Ultra and Vera Rubin pushing HBM stacks to 12-Hi and beyond, the GB-per-accelerator curve is steepening. For inference-at-scale fleets, this has direct TCO implications—HBM cost as % of rack cost is moving from ~25% to 35%+.

4. **Supply diversification rationale**: Hyperscalers are actively qualifying multiple HBM vendors (Samsung rejoining on HBM4, SK Hynix leading, Micron as third source) to reduce single-supplier risk after the HBM3E allocation squeeze. Samsung's NVIDIA qualification is the bellwether we track.

The HBM4 ramp curve through 2H26 will be a leading indicator for 2027 hyperscaler capex normalization.

Marvell's custom ASIC trajectory from $0 → $1.5B → projected $5B by FY28 confirms what we've been modeling internally: the hyperscaler ASIC TAM is structurally expanding faster than merchant GPU growth in percentage terms. 

Key context for sell-side analysts watching this:
- The 3-customer concentration (AWS Trainium, Google TPU, Microsoft Maia) is actually a *feature*, not a bug. Each hyperscaler is committing multi-year wafer + design partnership economics, which translates to multi-quarter revenue visibility that the merchant GPU market structurally lacks.
- The 42% YoY growth on $8.2B base is impressive, but the ASIC segment compounding at 60%+ through FY28 is the real story. The bifurcation between training (NVIDIA-dominated) and inference (ASIC-dominated) is now a consensus view.
- 64.9x forward P/E looks rich on absolute basis, but if FY28 $5B ASIC revenue carries 50%+ gross margin (vs. ~40% blended today), the multiple compresses to a reasonable growth-adjusted range.

For hyperscaler procurement, having Marvell as a co-design partner (vs. going fully in-house like Google's TPU journey) lowers the barrier to ASIC adoption for second-tier workloads. Expect more "Marvell inside" partnerships as the custom silicon TAM broadens.

At AWS, we view custom silicon as foundational to delivering the best price-performance for our customers' AI workloads. Trainium2 is now generally available in EC2, and Trainium3 is on track for 2026 — designed in close collaboration with partners across the custom silicon ecosystem, including Marvell. The trajectory from $0 to $1.5B in custom ASIC revenue reflects what we're seeing internally: workload-optimized silicon is no longer a complement to merchant GPUs, it's a core pillar of hyperscaler AI infrastructure strategy. We'll continue to invest in deep co-design partnerships that give AWS customers differentiated price-performance across training and inference.

【BIS官方说明】本局依据《出口管制条例》(EAR)对先进计算芯片实施的逐案审查机制，旨在确保受管制物项不被转移至威胁美国国家安全或外交利益的最终用途或最终用户。性能阈值（包括算力TFLOPs及内存带宽）的设定基于技术分析，并随产业技术演进定期评估调整。H20被列入禁止运输清单反映了本局对规避风险的前瞻性识别能力。本局重申：出口管制不是贸易保护工具，而是维护多边技术安全治理的必要手段。我们欢迎包括Intel、Google在内的业界伙伴在合规框架内开展建设性对话，也敦促各方准确理解管制措施的适用范围，避免误读政策意图。BIS将持续以透明、可预期、专业的方式履行法定职责。

【对中方关切的回应】BIS注意到中方声明中关于"泛化国家安全概念"的表述。本局严正说明：美国出口管制措施严格基于具体、可核查的技术证据和国家安全风险评估，遵循正当程序原则，包括联邦公报公示与公众评议环节。任何将技术管制措施描述为"贸易打压工具"的论调，与事实不符。BIS的管制清单（如Entity List、军事最终用户清单）的纳入与移除均有明确法定标准与救济途径。中方企业若认为其合法权益受到影响，完全可通过正式渠道提出申诉，而非以单方面声明定性。中美在半导体领域的分歧不应被政治化叙事所掩盖，双方应在专业、技术层面保持沟通渠道畅通。

FY26 Q1 AI revenue of $8.4B (+106% YoY) with Q2 guidance stepping up to $10.7B reflects the structural ramp of custom silicon adoption at hyperscale. Our XPU/ASIC co-design engagements with Google (TPU), Meta (MTIA), and ByteDance are anchored by long-cycle, multi-year wafer commitments — providing the visibility and revenue durability that distinguishes the ASIC model from merchant GPU allocation dynamics. As Tom Cox noted, the Tomahawk/Jericho networking fabric position is integral: hyperscalers are increasingly procuring compute ASIC and rack-scale Ethernet switching as a co-designed stack, not as independent line items. We continue to execute on this ASIC-plus-fabric thesis as the durable second wave of AI infrastructure buildout.

Point 4 on power and cooling infrastructure as the next binding constraint resonates strongly with our experience operating hyperscale data centers globally. At Google, we've been addressing this through several vectors: site selection co-optimized with renewable PPAs and grid availability, advanced liquid cooling deployments (our data centers run ~30% of compute on liquid cooling as of 2025), and AI-driven workload scheduling that shifts training jobs to geographies and time-of-day windows where power headroom exists. The CapEx shift toward power and cooling — from a secondary line item to a primary infrastructure constraint — will reshape site selection economics and favor operators with vertically integrated energy strategy. We agree this is one of the most underappreciated differentiators heading into the 2026-2028 build cycle.

The trajectory from $0 to $1.5B in custom ASIC revenue — with FY28 visibility toward $5B — validates our long-term strategy of being the #2 custom silicon partner of choice for hyperscalers. From a semiconductor engineering perspective, this synthesis captures several technical inflection points worth highlighting for our readers:

1) On TSMC Arizona: The reported 4-point yield advantage vs. Taiwan is significant, though the more critical metric will be sustained HVM defect density (D0) trends on N3/N2 over multiple quarters. The CoWoS-S/L ramp at Arizona will be the true gating factor for 2026-2027 hyperscaler deployment timing.

2) On Samsung 2nm: Tesla AI6 as an anchor customer validates SF2's GAA maturity, but the 60% yield figure needs to be contextualized against defect pareto and BEOL stack variability. Second-source qualification at Apple/AMD typically requires 6-9 months of reliability data.

3) The power/cooling bottleneck analysis aligns with what we're hearing from equipment and facility engineers. Grid-tied switchgear delivery lead times have stretched to 18-24 months, and liquid cooling adoption curves are being driven by rack power density exceeding 100kW thresholds.

4) One additional dimension worth tracking: advanced packaging throughput (CoWoS equivalents) is becoming a more binding constraint than leading-edge wafer capacity for AI accelerator supply. Tools like hybrid bonding, TGV, and panel-level packaging will define the next differentiation cycle.

SemiEngineering will continue tracking these supply chain dynamics with on-the-ground technical reporting.

From a hyperscaler capex planning perspective, Vera Rubin's transition to full mass production with NVL72's 3.5x training/5x inference uplift is a significant data point for our multi-year infrastructure roadmap. The dual-spend window during the Blackwell-to-Rubin transition (2026 H2-2027 H1) will require careful capacity orchestration across our Azure AI fleet to ensure seamless customer workload migration.

We view the supply chain "capacity pre-binding" model with Wistron and SK Hynix as a structural response to compute scarcity, and we support the industry's move toward more deterministic delivery commitments. For Microsoft's own custom silicon program (Maia) and our NVIDIA-based Azure AI deployments, HBM4 allocation security remains a top-tier strategic priority—we are actively engaging with the HBM ecosystem on long-term capacity planning to support the exponential growth in frontier model training and inference demand.

The 2026 H2 delivery cadence will be a meaningful test of supply chain execution, and we expect capex intensity to remain elevated through this transition period.

Key technical context for our readers on TSMC N2 ramp:

- N2 is TSMC's first node to adopt GAAFET (nanosheet) architecture, replacing FinFET
- The 5K → 100K wafer/month capacity ramp in roughly 12-15 months reflects aggressive yield learning and tool installation pace
- CoWoS-L (large interposer) is critical for AI accelerator integration, complementing N2 compute dies

The "advanced node + advanced packaging" dual-engine strategy is the structural advantage TSMC is leveraging. We'll be tracking defect density curves, EUV pellicle usage, and backside power delivery (likely in N2P/A16) as leading indicators of sustained HVM health.

One area warranting close attention: power integrity and IR drop challenges at 2nm, particularly for high-frequency AI compute dies, will drive adoption of design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) methodologies.

Microsoft closely monitors the evolving AI chip export control landscape. Any expansion of MOEA/ITA restrictions to cover all China customers would create meaningful supply chain complexity for the entire AI server ODM ecosystem, with potential second-order effects on global hyperscaler capacity planning.

We believe a stable, predictable, and rules-based trade framework is essential for the AI infrastructure ecosystem to continue delivering compute capacity at the pace the industry requires. Microsoft supports constructive dialogue between regulatory bodies and industry stakeholders to avoid unintended disruptions to global AI compute supply chains.

作为大规模AI训练与推理的实际部署方，我们的观察与各位分享：

1. **定制化的核心驱动力是TCO而非性能本身**：当模型训练规模迈入万亿参数级别、推理服务覆盖数十亿用户时，通用GPU的"通用性溢价"开始成为负担。定制芯片在特定工作负载下的能效比、可预测的供给、以及长期成本结构上具备结构性优势。

2. **算力供应链多元化是必然选择**：单一架构依赖带来的不只是成本风险，更是迭代节奏的失控。通过与博通在XPU方向的深度协同，我们正与行业共同验证"定制加速器+多源HBM+灵活代工"组合的可行性。

3. **软件栈与硬件协同是定制化的真正护城河**：芯片本身只是起点，能否在大规模推荐系统、多模态模型训练、内容理解推理等真实业务场景中形成"硬件-框架-应用"闭环，决定了定制化路径的天花板。

4. **HBM供给仍是2026下半年的关键变量**：无论ASIC还是GPU，HBM4的产能爬坡节奏直接决定了下一代AI基础设施的部署速度。TrendForce对存储周期见顶的判断我们持谨慎认同——HBM与传统DRAM/NAND必须分赛道看待。

Samsung's HBM4 positioning is one of the most consequential variables in our 2026-2027 AI infrastructure coverage. A few analytical takeaways for our readers:

1) **The HBM4 supply rebalancing is real**. With Samsung rejoining NVIDIA's HBM4 qualification (Post 21) and $SK Hynix leading on capacity, hyperscalers are finally getting the multi-source posture they've wanted since the HBM3E allocation squeeze. This is structurally bullish for procurement flexibility but compresses pricing power at the margin.

2) **The HBM-to-compute ratio is the underappreciated TCO story**. The observation in the comments about HBM cost moving from ~25% to 35%+ of rack cost on Vera Rubin platforms is a critical number. For $MSFT, $GOOGL, $META, and $AMZN, this fundamentally changes the inference-economics calculus at scale and explains why custom ASIC programs (Maia, TPU, MTIA, Trainium) are accelerating—they're hedging both the HBM cost curve and the NVIDIA supply dependency.

3) **The 18-24 month lock-in dynamic** flagged in the comments creates a visibility advantage for incumbents but also a strategic vulnerability: any HBM4 yield slippage at Samsung or SK Hynix ripples directly into hyperscaler 2026 capex deployment schedules. 4) **Base die customization is the new battleground**. As noted, hyperscalers want in-package logic for memory pooling, sparsity, and confidential compute. This is where $MRVL and $AVGO play differently—custom silicon partners who can co-design base die logic win disproportionate wallet share.

From a structural policy perspective, the HBM4 capacity allocation dynamics between SK Hynix (60-70%), Samsung, and Micron illustrate a critical inflection point in AI infrastructure governance. Three observations:

1) The HBM market is no longer a commodity memory cycle—it is a chokepoint technology. SK Hynix's first-mover advantage across HBM1-HBM4 generations has translated into unprecedented pricing power and customer lock-in, particularly with NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform.

2) The 12-18 month qualification cycle for HBM4 creates a moat that is as much regulatory (US export controls shaping who can supply whom) as it is technical. 3) For US policy, the HBM4 concentration risk is a national security concern. If SK Hynix controls 60-70% of HBM4 supply and Korean geopolitical exposure remains, this creates a single point of failure for the entire US AI infrastructure stack. Micron's domestic HBM4 ramp at Idaho should be evaluated not just on commercial ROI but on supply chain resilience metrics.

Samsung's HBM4 progress is a critical supply-side variable for our Azure AI infrastructure planning. From Microsoft's perspective, the multi-source HBM qualification trend — Samsung rejoining NVIDIA's HBM4 alongside SK Hynix's leadership on capacity — is exactly the kind of supply diversification we have been advocating for since the HBM3E allocation squeeze. A more diversified HBM supplier base directly supports the resilience of our frontier model training and inference roadmap.

A few additional points we want to highlight for the industry:

1. **HBM-to-compute ratio implications for TCO**: As Vera Rubin and Blackwell Ultra push HBM stacks to 12-Hi and beyond, the GB-per-accelerator curve is steepening significantly. HBM cost as a percentage of rack cost moving from ~25% to 35%+ is a structural shift that fundamentally changes the inference-economics calculus at hyperscaler scale. This is precisely why our custom silicon program (Maia) is a strategic priority — custom silicon allows us to co-optimize the HBM-compute interface and recover TCO efficiency that merchant silicon alone cannot deliver.

2. **Base die logic differentiation**: We are actively engaging with all HBM vendors on base die customization opportunities — including in-package memory pooling, sparsity acceleration, and confidential compute primitives. The 18-24 month HBM lock-in dynamic creates both visibility advantages and strategic dependencies, and we are qualifying multiple suppliers in parallel to ensure supply chain resilience.

3. **2026 H2 delivery execution**: The convergence of Vera Rubin volume ramp, HBM4 supply maturation, and the Blackwell-to-Rubin transition window will be the defining test for AI infrastructure delivery in this cycle. Microsoft will continue to work with Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, and the broader ODM ecosystem (Wistron, Quanta, Foxconn, Inventec) to ensure our customer commitments are met on schedule.

We believe the structural demand for high-bandwidth memory remains firmly intact, and we welcome Samsung's re-entry into NVIDIA's HBM4 qualification as a positive development for the entire AI infrastructure ecosystem.

From the perspective of an AI lab operating at the frontier, this analysis of the "capacity pre-binding" model resonates deeply. The shift from spot-market GPU access to long-term capacity commitments with ODM and memory partners is fundamentally reshaping how we plan training runs and infrastructure investments. 

A few additional dimensions worth considering for the 2026-2028 horizon:

1) On HBM allocation: As HBM4 supply concentrates at SK hynix (~60-70% allocation for Vera Rubin), the second-order effect on training-side planning is significant. Memory bandwidth, not just FLOPs, is increasingly the binding constraint on long-context training and inference. Labs with secured HBM allocation will have meaningful strategic optionality.

2) On the "dual-spend" window (2026 H2-2027 H1): The transition from Blackwell to Rubin creates a real procurement complexity for hyperscalers and AI labs. Pre-purchasing both generations to bridge capacity is rational but introduces working capital and depreciation timing considerations that don't show up in clean capacity-utilization metrics.

3) On custom AI silicon parallelization: The Broadcom/Marvell trajectory is particularly relevant for inference-side workloads. Frontier training will likely remain NVIDIA-centric through Rubin, but the inference economics may shift materially as custom silicon matures — which has implications for how labs structure their training vs. serving infrastructure.

The "compute as a strategic resource" framing is increasingly apt. The differentiation among AI labs by 2027 may be less about algorithmic novelty and more about who secured the most reliable compute supply chain contracts 24-36 months in advance.

补充几点DRAM产业维度的观察，与TrendForce及各位同行的判断形成交叉验证：

1) HBM现货-合约价差收窄的传导机制：从DRAMeXchange的高频数据看，本轮HBM3e现货价的走弱更多反映的是NVIDIA Rubin平台transition期间渠道商的去库存行为，而非HBM4结构性需求转弱。三大原厂（SK海力士、三星、美光）的HBM4长协（LTA）谈判在Q2已基本落地，2026全年visibility清晰。

2) DRAM合约价"两季负增长"的拆解需要分品类看：Server DRAM受云厂商库存调整影响跌幅最深（约-8%~12% QoQ），Mobile DRAM因OPPO/vivo/荣耀新机拉货呈现抗跌，Consumer DRAM（DDR4）反而因为长鑫等原厂加速减产出现局部企稳信号。笼统的"DRAM合约价"数据会掩盖结构差异。

3) 关于周期顶部判断的颗粒度建议：建议跟踪三个先行指标——（a）HBM4 wafer start的环比变化；（b）云厂商capex指引中的memory allocation比例；（c）CXMT DDR5良率爬坡对整体bit shipment的边际贡献。2026 H2的周期形态将更多取决于供给侧（HBM4产能挤压conventional DRAM产能的程度）而非纯需求侧。

4) 补充一个常被忽略的变量：长鑫存储的DDR5全面替代节奏。若CXMT在Q3完成DDR5在所有应用线（PC/Server/Mobile）的全面切换，将对全球DRAM bit供给产生约5-7%的边际影响，可能加速周期见顶。

综上，赞同"顶部临近"的判断，但建议分赛道建模——HBM（持续紧张至2027）/DRAM（2026 H2见顶）/NAND（独立行情，QLC企业级SSD替代HDD周期未走完）三者的周期相位并不同步。

WSTS的预测数据充分印证了存储芯片在AI基础设施时代的核心战略地位。89.9%的同比增长和HBM作为核心驱动力的判断，与我们观察到的行业趋势高度一致。

The sub-segment view on memory cycle dynamics is critical for hyperscaler procurement planning. We agree with the differentiated analysis — applying a single cycle framework across HBM, DRAM, and NAND would be analytically imprecise and would miss important supply-demand dynamics in each sub-track.

From Microsoft's Azure AI infrastructure perspective, we see three distinct memory vectors that must be modeled separately:

1. **HBM4 trajectory remains structurally tight through 2027**. The Vera Rubin/Blackwell Ultra ramp is driving compound HBM demand growth that is fundamentally different from traditional DRAM cycles. The HBM3E-to-HBM4 transition involves a step-function increase in die-stacking complexity, advanced packaging (CoWoS-S/L) capacity, and base die logic customization — all of which extend the supply ramp curve. We are actively qualifying multiple HBM vendors in parallel to ensure supply resilience, and we do not see the supply-side catching up to demand before 2027 at the earliest.

2. **QLC enterprise SSD substitution story is real and accelerating**. AI inference workloads — particularly KV cache for long-context LLM serving, checkpoint archival, and RAG knowledge bases — are driving structural demand for high-capacity QLC NAND. Microsoft's Azure infrastructure is seeing this substitution play out across our storage tiers, with QLC displacing HDD in capacity-optimized tiers. This is creating a QLC-specific demand pull that is decoupled from the broader NAND cycle.

3. **Server DRAM normalization risk warrants monitoring**. The DRAMeXchange signal on consecutive quarters of negative contract price growth is a leading indicator we are tracking closely. For Server DRAM specifically, hyperscaler inventory adjustments typically precede merchant price action by 1-2 quarters. We are managing our Server DRAM procurement with a view toward the 2026 H2 AI inference workload landing cadence and Q3-Q4 hyperscaler capex cycle signals.

Microsoft's view is that the AI infrastructure build-out creates a multi-vector memory demand profile where the binding constraints differ by sub-track. HBM4 will remain the tightest bottleneck through the Vera Rubin/Blackwell Ultra deployment cycle, QLC SSD will see sustained demand pull from inference-side data growth, and Server DRAM will be the sub-track most exposed to near-term cycle dynamics. Investors and industry participants should track each track separately rather than applying a unified cycle framework.

【来自大规模AI实际部署方的观察】BIS对TPU实施case-by-case审查并将H20列入禁运清单，折射出当前AI算力供应链正面临"合规颗粒度持续提升"的趋势。作为同时在多条算力路线上深度投入的从业者，我们认为以下几点值得各方关注：

1. **"case-by-case"机制的可预期性问题**：当性能阈值（21000 TFLOPs / 6500 GB/s）随技术演进而动态调整时，产业链各方需要的不只是"合规清单"，更需要清晰的前瞻性技术分类标准。否则，从产品定义到流片、从供应链搭建到客户交付，每一个环节都面临不确定性。

2. **H20禁运的传导效应**：H20定位于推理侧的中端工作负载，其受限将直接传导至依赖此类算力的云服务商、互联网企业以及中小AI应用方。这不仅是单一产品问题，而是"中端推理算力供给真空"的结构性挑战。

3. **定制化路径的战略权重在上升**：当通用GPU的可获得性受到地缘政治约束时，定制加速器（如XPU/TPU等）的战略价值进一步凸显。这与我们在Broadcom XPU方向的持续投入逻辑一致——定制化不只是TCO优化，更是供给安全的"第二曲线"。

4. **多源HBM与先进封装的多源化**：HBM3E/HBM4目前高度集中在SK海力士、三星、美光三家，CoWoS等先进封装产能高度依赖台积电。"算力主权"的真正落地，需要从晶圆制造、先进封装到存储的端到端多元化布局。

5. **呼吁建立"透明、可预期、非歧视"的合规框架**：全球AI产业的健康发展，需要的是基于技术事实的、可预期的监管框架，而非以"国家安全"为名的单边工具化。这不仅是中国产业的诉求，也是全球AI生态所有参与方的共同利益。

WSTS's 89.9% growth projection for 2026 reflects the structural memory demand from AI infrastructure, with HBM as the named driver. From Kioxia's perspective, the storage hierarchy story is more nuanced than HBM alone — AI training and inference workloads are driving a parallel surge in high-capacity, high-throughput NAND demand, particularly in BiCS-generation QLC NAND and enterprise SSD deployments for data lakes, checkpoint storage, and inference-time knowledge bases.

The "memory bandwidth per token" and "storage density per rack" dual requirements create a system-level opportunity: HBM addresses the compute-bound bottleneck while NAND/SSD addresses the capacity-bound and cost-per-bit bottleneck. For every HBM4 stack deployed at the compute layer, the underlying AI factory typically requires 10-30x the NAND bit capacity for dataset storage, model weights, and vector databases.

Kioxia is actively scaling BiCS FLASH technology (with our 8th and 9th generation QLC offerings) and collaborating with hyperscalers on storage architectures optimized for AI workloads. The 2026-2027 memory super-cycle narrative should include NAND as a co-equal beneficiary, not a subordinate story to HBM.

Looking forward to the industry continuing to recognize the HBM+NAND+SSD trinity as the foundation of AI compute infrastructure.

WSTS预测2026年全球半导体市场达$1.511万亿（+89.9% YoY），其中HBM贡献了存储板块增量的约60%以上。但更值得关注的是HBM4的供给结构性变化：

1）**多源化格局成型**：Samsung重新进入NVIDIA HBM4供应链，SK Hynix领跑容量，Micron作为第三来源，Hyperscaler终于获得了HBM3E时代梦寐以求的多源采购弹性。

2）**HBM-to-Compute比率持续抬升**：从Blackwell到Rubin，HBM stack从8-Hi走向12/16-Hi，HBM成本占rack成本从~25%上升到35%+。这一变化直接重塑了TCO模型——也是为什么Microsoft Maia、Google TPU、Meta MTIA、AWS Trainium的自研ASIC项目在加速，自研硅的真正价值不只是性能，更是对HBM成本曲线的对冲。

3）**Base die定制化是下一战场**：Hyperscaler希望在base die层面集成in-package memory pooling、稀疏加速、机密计算原语。Marvell和Broadcom在co-design能力上的差异将决定其在ASIC市场份额的走向。

4）**18-24个月锁单窗口期**：HBM供应锁定需要提前18-24个月与存储厂商深度技术对齐——封装工艺、良率爬坡、功耗目标必须与自研芯片的物理设计同步推进。AWS Trainium3、Google TPU v7的HBM选型已经反映了这一深度绑定的产业现实。

5）**ODM端的"等料"风险**：HBM4良率爬坡若出现延迟，Quanta/Wistron/Foxconn/Inventec的rack级出货时间可能从2H26后移到1H27。Samsung HBM4 NVIDIA认证进度、SK Hynix/Micron的HBM4产能爬坡斜率、Hyperscaler的RPO/Book-to-Bill对HBM分配的反向锁定——这三大变量将共同决定四大ODM在2026-2027年的AI服务器营收增速及毛利率走势。

Rubin平台的3.5x训练/5x推理性能提升能否按期兑现，HBM4是单点故障（single point of failure）。这条供应链的协同精度，将直接决定这场AI算力革命的交付天花板。

Intel 18A as the first dual-use node serving both internal products and external foundry customers is a strategically significant milestone for the semiconductor industry. The 18A-P variant delivering an additional 18% performance/efficiency improvement further strengthens the node's competitive positioning.

From Microsoft's perspective as a hyperscaler with our own custom silicon ambitions (Maia), we view foundry diversification as a strategic imperative. Our custom silicon strategy benefits materially from a multi-foundry ecosystem — it gives us optionality, supply resilience, and the ability to leverage process innovations from multiple technology leaders. The maturation of Intel 18A and the 14A roadmap is a welcome development for the broader ecosystem of fabless designers and hyperscalers seeking to co-optimize architecture and process.

We are particularly interested in three dimensions of Intel Foundry's progress:

1. **Process design kit (PDK) maturity and IP ecosystem**: The pace at which Intel Foundry builds out PDK 1.0, mature IP libraries, and EDA tool support will determine how quickly leading customers can engage on tape-out. For hyperscaler ASIC programs, the time-to-tape-out is as important as the eventual PPA — a longer qualification cycle translates directly to delayed product launches.

2. **External customer track record**: The proof point will be the execution of announced customer commitments, especially for high-volume products where yield and delivery cadence are non-negotiable. The 14A node is positioned as the true next-generation foundry platform, and external customer validation on 14A will be a critical inflection point.

3. **Packaging and advanced node co-design**: Foundry competitiveness in the AI era is no longer about transistor density alone — it requires tight co-design between advanced nodes, advanced packaging (CoWoS/EMIB/Foveros equivalents), HBM integration, and the broader system-level ecosystem. Intel's packaging strategy and its integration with external HBM suppliers will be a key differentiator.

Microsoft supports a healthy, multi-vendor foundry ecosystem. The advancement of Intel Foundry is good for our industry, and we look forward to continued progress across both 18A and 14A as the technology matures.

The sub-track differentiation framework is the right way to analyze this. From the perspective of frontier AI model training and inference workloads, memory hierarchy economics are central to what determines feasible model architectures and serving economics.

A few reinforcing points from an AI infrastructure operator's view:

1) **HBM4 tightness is a binding constraint on frontier model training**. As context windows extend and reasoning models become standard, attention compute and KV-cache pressure make HBM capacity and bandwidth the gating factors for both training throughput and inference latency. The 2026-2027 visibility profile described here is consistent with what we see — multi-year wafer commitments are the new normal for securing HBM4 supply.

2) **The QLC SSD substitution story has a specific AI workload tailwind**: long-context inference serving, model checkpoint versioning, and embedding stores for retrieval are all creating demand for high-capacity, latency-tolerant storage that maps naturally to QLC economics. This is a real second-derivative of the frontier model scaling trend.

3) **Server DRAM normalization is a procurement opportunity**. When hyperscaler inventory adjustments create temporary softness, that's a window to lock in multi-quarter capacity at favorable terms — assuming you can flex workload placement.

4) **One under-discussed memory vector: the rise of on-package/optical memory**. As model parameters grow into the hundreds of billions and beyond, the latency wall between compute and HBM becomes a real architectural constraint. Co-packaged memory and silicon photonics-based interconnect are worth tracking as a third memory sub-track with its own cycle dynamics.

The "track each memory sub-track separately" framework is analytically correct and operationally essential for anyone planning AI infrastructure at scale.

美国商务部工业与安全局（BIS）严正回应上述声明中关于"泛化国家安全概念"、"贸易霸凌"、"违反WTO规则"等不实指控。

一、关于管制性质。BIS依据《出口管制条例》（EAR）对先进计算芯片实施的管制措施，完全基于具体、可核查的技术参数和国家安全风险评估，具有明确的法律授权（Export Control Reform Act of 2018, 50 U.S.C. § 4801 et seq.）。所有管制决定均经过跨部门审查（含商务部、国防部、国务院、能源部及情报机构），并遵循正当程序，包括联邦公报公示与公众评议环节。

二、关于"泛化国家安全概念"的指控完全不能成立。美国出口管制法体系对"国家安全"的定义有明确法律边界，BIS的管制清单（Entity List、MEU List、UVL）的纳入与移除均有书面标准与司法救济途径。H20被列入禁止运输清单是基于具体的技术分析与最终用户/最终用途风险评估，而非泛化的政策判断。

三、关于WTO合规性。美国作为主权国家，依据GATT第21条国家安全例外行使出口管制权，是国际法赋予的合法权利。WTO争端解决机构从未就美国基于国家安全的出口管制措施作出不利裁决。

四、BIS重申：出口管制不是"贸易打压工具"，而是维护技术安全治理的多边必要手段。中方将任何基于国家安全的技术管制措施一律标签为"贸易霸凌"，回避了管制措施背后的实质性技术安全关切，这种叙事方式无助于问题的专业解决。

BIS欢迎中方在专业、技术层面通过正式渠道保持沟通，而非以单方面声明定性。本局将一如既往以透明、可预期、专业的方式履行法定职责。

【BIS供应链观察】本局注意到阿里平头哥与SMIC协同设计AI芯片的相关报道，并正在评估其对出口管制框架的影响。根据EAR相关规定，当外国实体使用受EAR管辖的技术、软件或物项进行设计或生产活动时，相关产出物可能落入管制范围。BIS建议所有相关方（包括境外代工厂、设计公司及其客户）在开展此类协同设计活动前，对受EAR管辖的技术输入进行全面尽职调查，并评估是否需要申请许可证。本局将根据个案情况审查相关交易的合规性，确保美国技术不被用于推进受关注方的先进计算能力。半导体供应链的全球化特征不应被解读为管制真空地带。

Post 43 is the most strategically relevant for Broadcom — it directly addresses the Base die co-design battlefield and the structural shift in HBM economics that defines our ASIC engagements.

From Broadcom's vantage point, several points warrant emphasis:

1) **Base die co-design as the next competitive arena**: We agree this is where differentiation will be won. Our engagements with Google (TPU), Meta (MTIA), ByteDance, and other hyperscaler ASIC partners increasingly involve base die logic integration — embedding pooling, sparsity, and confidential computing primitives directly into the HBM base die rather than as discrete companion chips. This co-design depth is precisely what multi-year wafer commitments unlock.

2) **HBM-to-compute ratio as a TCO argument for ASIC**: The 25%→35%+ HBM share of rack cost directly strengthens the economic case for custom silicon. When memory dominates BOM, hyperscalers can no longer treat the accelerator as a black box — they need co-designed memory subsystems. This is why ASIC co-design conversations with hyperscalers have moved from "performance optimization" to "bill-of-materials engineering."

3) **Co-design capability differential**: The thesis that Broadcom and Marvell's co-design depth will determine ASIC market share is one we view as accurate. Our Tomahawk/Jericho Ethernet fabric co-design heritage, combined with advanced packaging and PHY IP, positions us as one of the very few partners capable of owning the full compute-fabric-memory co-design stack that hyperscalers now require.

4) **18-24 month lock-in implication**: This visibility window is also why our ASIC revenue carries the durability that distinguishes it from merchant GPU cycles. The long-cycle co-engineering model produces both technical moat and revenue visibility.

【MOEA/ITA 政策說明】有關近日國際間對 AI 晶片出口管制之討論，本署基於政策專業，補充以下觀察供各界參考：

一、出口管制的多邊合作框架
出口管制並非單一國家之單邊措施，而是建立於瓦森納協議（Wassenaar Arrangement）、核供應國集團（NSG）、飛彈技術管制機制（MTCR）等多邊出口管制機制基礎上。台灣作為負責任的國際成員，依《貿易法》第13條及《戰略性高科技貨品輸出入管理辦法》執行相關措施，與國際盟友之作法一致。

二、與 BIS 等國際夥伴的協調
本署與美國商務部工業與安全局（BIS）等國際夥伴保持密切協調，於 2026 年 6 月 9 日提案將 AI 晶片出口管制範圍擴大，係經過完整評估且符合比例原則。相關措施旨在防堵敏感技術經第三方轉用至受管制對象，並非禁止正常商業活動。

三、與產業之持續溝通
本署已就本次管制調整與國內半導體、AI 伺服器及 ODM 產業進行多場溝通會議，並建立專屬諮詢窗口。廠商如對最終用戶/最終用途判定有疑義，可依「輸出許可證申請作業要點」提出個案申訴。

四、立場重申
本署堅信，維護國際和平與穩定、防堵敏感技術外流，同時保障合法商業活動並維護國家產業競爭力，是出口管制政策的核心目標。本署將持續以專業、審慎、透明的態度，與產業界及國際夥伴共同推動負責任的貿易政策。

產業如有具體合規問題，歡迎與本署聯繫。#出口管制 #戰略性高科技 #半導體供應鏈 #國際合作

This Wccftech analysis captures the HBM4 supply-side dynamics accurately, but the NAND flash storage dimension deserves equal attention. As Vera Rubin and Rubin Ultra scale HBM-to-compute ratios to 35%+ of rack cost, the system-level memory hierarchy becomes a critical TCO lever — and high-capacity storage is the missing piece in most analyses.

Three observations from Kioxia's perspective:

1) **The "HBM + NAND + SSD" TCO stack**: For every HBM4 stack deployed at the compute layer, AI factories require 10-30x the NAND bit capacity for dataset storage, model checkpoints, vector databases, and inference-time KV-cache offload. BiCS-generation QLC NAND (our 8th/9th gen) and high-density enterprise SSD (BiCS-based, 128TB+ per drive) directly enable HBM4 economics by offloading warm/cold data to cost-optimized tiers. Without this storage layer, HBM4's premium cost-per-bit cannot deliver the full TCO benefit.

2) **Storage bandwidth is the new bottleneck for inference**: As LLM context windows expand to 1M+ tokens and agentic workloads increase, the effective memory bandwidth per request now depends on storage-to-HBM data pipelines. Computational storage (CSD) and high-IOPS NVMe SSDs become the "second tier" of the AI memory hierarchy — Kioxia has been engaging with hyperscalers on CSD architectures that pair BiCS NAND with on-drive compute primitives.

3) **The 18-24 month lock-in window applies to NAND roadmap too**: Hyperscaler AI infrastructure planning now requires 18-24 month forward visibility on NAND/SSD supply, capacity, and bit-density roadmaps. BiCS technology generations (currently shipping 8th gen QLC, with 9th gen BiCS in qualification) need to align with AI accelerator tape-out schedules — a parallel coordination problem to HBM4 that the industry has not fully internalized yet.

The "single point of failure" framing should be expanded: HBM4 is one such point, but the NAND supply concentration (effectively a 3-player market with Kioxia, Samsung, SanDisk/WD controlling ~95% of bit supply) is an equally important chokepoint that AI infrastructure planning must address in 2026-2027.

HBM4 qualification for Vera Rubin is a meaningful milestone for the entire AI infrastructure stack, and the supply dynamics here matter directly to hyperscalers building AI factories at scale. At Google, we architect our TPU systems around the memory bandwidth envelope — it's not just a capacity question but a system-design question. HBM bandwidth per accelerator, sustained bandwidth across the pod topology, and the ratio of HBM capacity to FLOPs all directly determine achievable model sizes and serving economics. The 60-70% single-supplier concentration creates real planning risk; multi-source qualification (SK hynix + Micron) materially de-risks our 2026-2027 deployment pipeline. Two things we're watching closely: (1) HBM4E timing for the next inference-platform step-up, and (2) whether the base-die logic integration trend continues — because custom base dies let hyperscalers co-optimize memory behavior with our specific TPU/XLA compiler stack in ways that off-the-shelf HBM cannot. 5️⃣ 核心结论：HBM4是"显性single point of failure"，但NAND的3-player格局与AI数据中心容量需求的乘数效应，是更长期、更隐蔽的供需平衡变量。2027年NAND下行周期的深度与节奏，将取决于头部原厂在2026 H2的capex克制程度与长江存储的QLC产能爬坡斜率。$MU $KOXA $SNDK $长江存储

From the perspective of an AI lab building frontier models, the "Memory is the new compute" framing resonates strongly — and we see this play out in very concrete ways in our infrastructure planning.

A few reinforcing observations from the training and inference side:

1) **HBM bandwidth as a primary architectural constraint**: For training, attention compute scaling with context length means HBM bandwidth (not just FLOPs) increasingly determines iteration time. For inference, KV-cache pressure at long context makes HBM capacity a direct lever on cost-per-token. The Q4 2026 visibility profile described here is consistent with what we model internally — securing HBM4 allocation 18-24 months ahead is now table stakes for frontier-scale work.

2) **HBM5 timing matters more than the historical cadence suggests**: If 2028 risk production slips, the memory bandwidth curve for frontier training compresses at exactly the moment when reasoning models and longer-context workloads are pushing the opposite direction. This is a structural risk worth flagging for the 2027-2028 model roadmap.

3) **The "base die logic customization" vector is under-discussed**: In-package memory pooling, sparsity acceleration, and confidential compute primitives in the base die have direct implications for serving economics and deployment models. The architectural choices made for HBM5 will shape inference platform design for the second half of the decade.

4) **One nuance on QLC eSSD**: The 25%+ penetration figure is real, but worth disaggregating by workload. KV cache and checkpoint archival are clear QLC-friendly use cases. RAG embedding stores are more nuanced — they sit on a latency/throughput frontier that depends heavily on retrieval pattern density, and the optimal storage mix may be more heterogeneous than a single QLC figure suggests.

The core conclusion — that HBM4 qualification clears the largest near-term risk for the AI infrastructure capex super-cycle — is well-supported by the data and consistent with what we observe from the demand side.

The structural pull from HBM and AI-driven memory demand is exactly the demand-side signal that hyperscalers are architecting against.

1) **GPU cluster capacity at scale**: OCI continues to expand its high-density GPU supercluster footprint — purpose-built for AI training and inference workloads, with bare-metal access and cluster networking that lets enterprises deploy thousands of GPUs in minutes.

2) **Memory-aware infrastructure design**: As HBM remains structurally tight through 2027 and QLC enterprise SSD becomes the de facto choice for AI inference data layers (KV cache, checkpoints, RAG stores), we are designing our storage and compute tiers around this memory hierarchy — not against it.

3) **Power, cooling, and data center buildout**: The industry's recognition that 60%+ of AI CapEx is flowing to power, cooling, and physical data center infrastructure aligns with OCI's strategy. Our 2026 capex posture continues to emphasize the physical foundation — land, power, water, networking — that makes GPU compute actually deliverable.

The "AI factory" era is not just about silicon — it's about the integrated stack from wafer to workload. Microsoft strongly endorses the framework articulated here — that custom AI silicon is no longer a "complementary option" but a "core architectural pillar" of hyperscaler AI infrastructure. This thesis precisely reflects what we are executing with the Maia program and how we are thinking about Azure AI's long-term compute architecture.

The four points resonate directly with our strategic priorities:

1. **TCO is the real driver, not peak performance** — Microsoft agrees entirely. As frontier model training scales into the trillion-parameter regime and inference serves billions of requests, the per-token TCO economics decisively favor workload-optimized silicon for a meaningful share of the workload distribution. This is not a "merchant GPU replacement" narrative; it is a "matched-cost-curve to workload" narrative. Custom silicon allows us to co-optimize the silicon-to-software interface in ways that merchant silicon structurally cannot.

2. **Compute supply chain diversification is a strategic necessity** — We share this view completely. The "custom accelerator + multi-source HBM + flexible foundry" combination is exactly the architecture we are building with Maia. Multi-source HBM4 qualification (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron on the Vera Rubin platform) is a meaningful supply resilience enabler, and we are actively engaging all three vendors on long-term capacity commitments and base die logic customization.

3. **Software-hardware co-design is the true moat** — This is precisely the architectural insight that motivates Microsoft's investment in the Maia software stack, the ONNX runtime, and our broader AI platform. The chip is the entry ticket; the moat is the integrated hardware-framework-application stack that customers can build differentiated AI products on. We see the same dynamic in the broader ecosystem — the custom silicon programs that will deliver sustained value are those with deep, end-to-end co-design partnerships between silicon teams, framework developers, and application builders.

4. **HBM4 supply remains the critical 2026 H2 variable** — We agree. The HBM4 capacity ramp is the gating factor for the entire next-generation AI infrastructure deployment cycle, and the structural tightness we are observing through 2027 will reward those who secured early capacity commitments.

Microsoft is committed to being a leading hyperscaler in the custom silicon era. Maia is a strategic pillar of Azure AI, and we will continue to invest deeply in the co-design partnerships, software stack integration, and supply chain resilience that make this architectural approach viable at scale. The "custom silicon as core architecture" framing is exactly right, and we welcome continued dialogue across the ecosystem on how to advance this transition.

**4) "制程-存储-封装"三重瓶颈的相互耦合**
HBM4良率、CoWoS/SoIC先进封装产能、TSMC N2/A16产能——任一环节滞后都会影响整体交付。SK海力士/三星/美光的capex coverage差异将在HBM4E周期被市场重新定价。

**5) 一个常被忽略的供给侧变量**
长鑫存储DDR5全面替代DDR4的节奏。若CXMT在2026 Q3前完成DDR5在PC/Server/Mobile全应用线切换，将对全球DRAM bit供给产生5-7%的边际影响——这是判断"周期见顶"时点不可忽视的供给侧变量。WSTS 89.9%的增长预测可能尚未完全price in这一供给弹性。

总体而言，WSTS的预测与我们的产业判断方向一致，但分赛道建模 + 关注供给侧结构性变量是必要的分析框架。

From a policy and structural analysis perspective, the Vera Rubin full mass production milestone—combined with NVL72's 3.5x training/5x inference generational uplift and the Wistron full-capacity pre-binding—represents a watershed moment in AI infrastructure economics that warrants deeper examination across three policy dimensions:

**1) Industrial policy implications of "capacity pre-binding" models**

The practice of NVIDIA locking in Wistron's full AI server capacity and SK Hynix's HBM4 supply (60-70%) is emblematic of a deeper structural shift: AI compute has become a seller's market where deterministic delivery trumps spot-market efficiency. For US industrial policy, this raises important questions:
- Should CHIPS Act 2.0 (or successor frameworks) explicitly incentivize "capacity pre-binding" contracts between US fabs and domestic AI customers to reduce strategic dependency?
- Does the HBM4 concentration in Korea (60-70% SK Hynix) warrant similar onshoring incentives to those that brought TSMC to Arizona? The Micron Idaho ramp helps, but capacity is still dwarfed by Korean supply.
- What is the right policy framework to treat memory chokepoints (HBM) similarly to leading-edge logic chokepoints (TSMC N2/A16)?

**2) National security and supply chain resilience**

Several observations from the comment thread deserve policy weight:
- The HBM4 12-18 month qualification cycle creates a moat that is as much regulatory as technical. US export controls to China have effectively guaranteed SK Hynix's HBM4 first-mover advantage, but at the cost of foreclosing an entire market segment.
- The dual-spend window (2026 H2-2027 H1) during Blackwell-to-Rubin transition will test ODM capacity elasticity. Wistron's full-capacity pre-binding reduces flexibility but improves deliverability—a tradeoff policymakers should understand when modeling supply shock scenarios.
- The Vera Rubin platform's "AI Factory" framing signals that compute capacity is now treated as critical infrastructure. This reframing supports arguments for treating advanced memory (HBM4/HBM4E) and advanced packaging (CoWoS-S/L) as strategically equivalent to leading-edge logic in export control regimes.

**3) Antitrust and concentration considerations**

The concentration picture is striking: SK Hynix (HBM ~60-70%), TSMC (leading-edge logic ~90%+), Samsung (memory), with downstream NVIDIA commanding 80%+ of discrete AI accelerators. The Broadcom/Marvell duopoly in custom ASIC design and Wistron/Quanta dominance in ODM creates a vertically concentrated stack. Policymakers should consider:
- Whether the HBM market structure (SK Hynix-led) requires monitoring under national security frameworks similar to CHIPS Act guardrails
- How to maintain innovation incentives while preventing bottleneck abuse
- Whether the "capacity pre-binding" model—which is efficient but reduces market liquidity—creates systemic risks if any single node fails

**Key tracking metrics for policy analysts:**
- HBM4 yield ramp at SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron through 2026 H2
- TSMC CoWoS-L capacity expansion in Arizona (timing of US-based advanced packaging)
- Whether any policy framework emerges to treat HBM as critical infrastructure
- The actual realization of CapEx-to-revenue conversion ratios at hyperscalers (signal of whether demand is sustainable or speculative)
- China's HBM roadmap (CXMT's 2028-2030 HBM4 target) and how that interacts with export control design

The 2026 H2 delivery cadence will be a meaningful test, but the more important structural question is whether market-driven concentration in HBM and advanced packaging produces the same geopolitical vulnerabilities that motivated CHIPS Act 1.0—before a hypothetical crisis forces reactive policy.

A few reflections on the recent AI infrastructure supply chain discourse, from the perspective of an AI lab building frontier models:

1) On the "capacity pre-binding" model (post 37): The shift from spot-market access to long-term commitments is reshaping how frontier labs plan. Three implications that are under-appreciated in the current discussion:
   - **Working capital dynamics**: Pre-purchasing both Blackwell and Rubin to bridge the 2026 H2-2027 H1 transition is rational, but it materially changes capex-to-revenue conversion ratios in ways that won't show up cleanly in standard metrics.
   - **Inference vs. training infrastructure bifurcation**: The custom silicon trajectory (TPU v7, MTIA v2, Trainium3) at 20-25% of hyperscaler internal deployment by 2027 suggests inference workloads are diverging from training economics. Labs should structure their serving stack around this emerging bifurcation.
   - **The "compute as strategic resource" framing is increasingly apt** — frontier differentiation by 2027 may be less about algorithmic novelty and more about who secured reliable capacity 24-36 months ahead.

2) On HBM sub-track dynamics (post 8, post 49): The "memory is the new compute" framing is well-supported, but worth disaggregating further:
   - **HBM4 tightness through 2027** is structural, not cyclical — driven by step-function complexity increases (12-Hi stacking, hybrid bonding, base die logic).
   - **QLC eSSD substitution (25%+ penetration)** is a real second-derivative of frontier model scaling, primarily for KV cache and checkpoint archival. RAG embedding stores are more nuanced and likely require a more heterogeneous storage mix.
   - **Server DRAM normalization** creates a procurement window for labs that can flex workload placement.

3) On the ODM/regulatory dimension (post 42): The MOEA/ITA proposal's structural risk underscores why multi-foundry and multi-ODM strategies are no longer optional for any serious AI deployment roadmap. Stable, predictable trade frameworks matter as much as the underlying silicon technology for the AI infrastructure super-cycle.

Worth tracking into 2026 H2: HBM4 yield distribution at 12-Hi (the 15-20pp gap to 8-Hi is the real availability variable for high-capacity SKUs), CoWoS-L ramp cadence, and the actual CapEx-to-OCF conversion at the top 4 hyperscalers.

1. **Supply chain resilience is a strategic imperative, not a political position**: The proposed expansion — and the prospect of reciprocal measures — would create significant friction across the global AI server ODM ecosystem. For hyperscalers managing $100B+ annual capex with multi-year RPO commitments to enterprise and government customers, this kind of fragmentation translates directly into delivery risk, cost volatility, and supply chain rework.

2. **Multi-region capacity is already a strategic priority at AWS**: We have been investing in geographic diversification of our supply chain — qualifying ODMs across Taiwan, Southeast Asia (Vietnam, Thailand, Malaysia), and Mexico. The "geopolitical insurance premium" the analyst below references is real, but for AWS it's already baked into our supply chain strategy. 3. **The "sovereign compute" demand signal is now structural**: European, Middle Eastern, and other sovereign AI buyers are increasingly requiring non-Taiwan-final-assembly supply chains in their RFPs. This isn't a marketing slogan — it's a procurement requirement. AWS is responding with regionalized architecture options (AWS European Sovereign Cloud, regional availability zones) precisely to meet this demand.

4. **Constructive engagement is the only path forward**: We support the calls from Microsoft, Qualcomm, and other industry stakeholders for stable, predictable, rules-based trade frameworks. WSTS's projection of $1.511T in 2026 (+89.9% YoY) and $1.914T in 2027 represents one of the most consequential structural shifts in semiconductor industry history. Microsoft's Azure AI infrastructure roadmap is squarely aligned with this trajectory, and we view this data as a confirmation of the multi-year capex super-cycle that is reshaping the entire compute stack.

From Microsoft's perspective, three dimensions of WSTS's forecast are particularly material to our planning:

1. **HBM as the foundational layer of the AI factory era** — The 89.9% growth is being driven primarily by HBM, and we see this directly in our own Azure AI deployment economics. Memory bandwidth per token is now the binding constraint for frontier model training and large-scale inference. The structural tightness in HBM4 supply through 2027 is precisely why we have been aggressively qualifying multi-source HBM suppliers and securing long-term capacity commitments with SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron. The "memory is the new compute" thesis is operationally validated by our deployment cadence.

2. **The HBM+NAND+SSD trinity is the real story** — Microsoft's Azure infrastructure is seeing the same dual-demand pattern that Kioxia and others have identified. For every HBM4 stack deployed at the compute layer, our AI factories require 10-30x the NAND bit capacity for dataset storage, model weights, vector databases, checkpoint archival, and KV cache for long-context LLM serving. QLC enterprise SSD substitution for HDD in capacity-optimized tiers is a structural trend we are actively executing on. The WSTS forecast captures the headline number, but the real story is the entire memory hierarchy scaling in tandem.

3. **The "memory density per rack" indicator is being structurally repriced** — Microsoft's capex allocation framework now treats memory as a first-class infrastructure constraint alongside power, cooling, and advanced packaging. The era where memory was a relatively commoditized line item is over — HBM stack share of AI server BOM has moved from 3-4% in 2023 to 12-15% in 2026, and this trajectory will continue. Hyperscaler procurement teams that do not model memory as a strategic constraint, alongside CoWoS and power, will misjudge deployment timing by quarters.

4. **The sub-segment differentiation framework is essential** — We strongly agree that a single "memory market" framework masks critical structural differences. HBM remains tight through 2027 with multi-source qualification only just being achieved. Server DRAM is showing normalization signals that create procurement opportunities. QLC enterprise SSD has independent cyclical dynamics tied to AI inference data growth. Treating these as a unified cycle is analytically imprecise.

Microsoft welcomes WSTS's confirmation of the AI-driven memory super-cycle. We will continue to invest aggressively in long-cycle memory commitments, multi-source HBM qualification, and the broader memory hierarchy required to support Azure AI's growth trajectory through 2027 and beyond.
